canonical_statement: The study evaluated the long-term efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin monotherapy over 102 weeks in treatment-naive people with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise.

population.label: Drug-naive adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise in the main morning-dose cohort

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults aged 18–77 years with type 2 diabetes.

population.label: Adults aged 18–77 years with type 2 diabetes

canonical_statement: Participants in the main cohort were treatment-naive and had inadequate glycaemic control with diet and exercise alone.

population.label: Treatment-naive adults inadequately controlled with diet and exercise
inclusion_criteria: Inadequate glycaemic control with diet and exercise

canonical_statement: The main cohort required baseline HbA1c 53–86 mmol/mol (7.0–10.0%).
The paper reports the morning-dose main cohort rather than the exploratory higher-HbA1c/evening-dose cohorts because U.S. prescribing information specified morning administration.
The reported main cohort randomized 274 participants: placebo n=75, dapagliflozin 2.5 mg n=65, 5 mg n=64, and 10 mg n=70.

population.label: Drug-naive adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise in the main morning-dose cohort

canonical_statement: Baseline mean HbA1c was similar across groups, ranging from 7.84% to 8.01%.
Most participants were overweight or obese: 92.0–98.6% had BMI ≥25 kg/m² and 59.4–72.9% had BMI ≥30 kg/m² across randomized groups.
The cohort was predominantly White (90.0–96.9% across groups), limiting racial diversity.
The population had relatively early type 2 diabetes, with mean disease duration approximately 1.0–2.3 years across groups.
Of 274 randomized participants in the main cohort, 167 completed the 102-week study (60.9%).
Participants assigned to dapagliflozin 2.5 mg received oral dapagliflozin once daily in the morning for up to 102 weeks.
Participants assigned to dapagliflozin 5 mg received oral dapagliflozin once daily in the morning for up to 102 weeks.
Participants assigned to dapagliflozin 10 mg received oral dapagliflozin once daily in the morning for up to 102 weeks.

The control group received matching placebo through week 24; for ethical reasons, blinded metformin 500 mg/day was added after week 24, yielding a placebo-plus-low-dose-metformin comparator through week 102.

exposures.details: Matching placebo through week 24; blinded metformin 500 mg/day added from week 24 through week 102.

canonical_statement: This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 study conducted at 85 centers in Canada, Mexico, Russia, and the United States between September 2007 and July 2010.

canonical_statement: No thromboembolic events were reported despite small proportions of dapagliflozin-treated participants reaching haematocrit >55%.
A substantial proportion of participants discontinued or received rescue therapy by week 102, reducing the amount of untreated efficacy data available for long-term comparison.
Excluding post-rescue efficacy measurements avoids contamination by rescue therapy but reduces observations over time; the mixed-model analysis assumes missing data are missing at random.
The trial was powered for the week-24 primary endpoint rather than the extension; week-102 P values were post hoc nominal tests without multiplicity adjustment.
The week-102 comparator was no longer pure placebo because low-dose metformin 500 mg/day was added after week 24, complicating interpretation of long-term placebo-controlled effects.

The authors concluded that dapagliflozin monotherapy provided durable glycaemic improvement and weight reduction over 102 weeks without increasing hypoglycaemia, supporting dapagliflozin as a possible initial pharmacotherapy option for type 2 diabetes.
